Kryve Ozero Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Kryve Ozero's Jewish community, first mentioned in 1765, grew to 5,478 people (70 percent) by 1897, supporting six synagogues by 1910. In December 1919, a weeks-long pogrom carried out by the Volunteer Army killed nearly 600 Jews and drove some 600 families to leave the town. After the August 1941 occupation, most remaining Jews were deported to the Bohdanivka camp; the last 186 were murdered on January 1, 1942. In the 1980s, victims were reburied in this cemetery and a monument erected.
